title: Introduction to Food Science and Technology
requirements: Co-requisite: BCHE2030.
description: This course will provide an overview of various topics in food science and technology. Lectures will include discussions of general areas of interest chosen to stimulate and foster students' interest in both food science and food technology. The course will cover topics that include basic food chemistry, food processing and preservation, food microbiology and fermentation, food safety and toxicology, food engineering, food biotechnology, food evaluation and product development, etc. Relevant examples will be cited to strengthen the basic understanding of the principles in each topic. Local issues related to food will also be discussed.
outcome: -Define Food Science and Food Technology -Understand the dimensions of food processing and preservation -Grasp the basic information in food chemistry, food microbiology and food product development, and be able to utilize them in the preparation of safe and high quality food products -Tell the current trends and advancements in Food Science and Technology
syllabus: -Introduction and Food Science and Technology -Food categories and composition -Food chemistry -Food additives -Food processing and preservation -Food microbiology and fermentation -Food safety and toxicology -Food biotechnology -Sensory evaluation and food product development

title: Nutrition for Health
requirements: Pre-requisite: FNSC2001.
description: This course provides an overview of the basic concepts and principles of nutrition science and how to apply the principles of good nutrition in everyday life to the planning of healthy eating for optimal health, performance and disease prevention. Students will also be able to identify some common Hong Kong nutrition problems and the role of nutrition in their origins, prevention and therapy. The course will also expose the students to some additional nutritional issues of current health or research significance.
outcome: -Define the science of nutrition, and discuss the importance of nutritional adequacy and balance for optimal growth and health -Identify the dietary sources, functions and key roles in health protection of the major nutrients -Discuss the health effects of the major nutrients in terms of deficiency and excess -Identify some common Hong Kong nutritional problems and some current nutritional issues of health or research significance -Interpret the common media presentations of nutrition information-valid or flawed? -Apply the principles of good nutrition in their own lives to the planning of healthy eating for optimal performance and disease prevention
syllabus: -Nutrition Recommendation -Macro- & Micro-nutrients -Nutrition & Non-communicable Diseases -Healthy Eating
recommended_readings: -Gibney M.J. et al. 2009. Introduction to Human Nutrition (2nd ed.), Wiley-Blackwell, Ames, Iowa, USA (UL QU145I665 2009).

title: Ethics and Professionalism for Nutritionists
description: Ethics are principles that governing a person’s professional behaviour. Students need to understand what is and what is not professional behaviour. Therefore, this course will cover the issues of professional behavior, including Association for Nutrition (AfN) Standards for Ethics, Conduct and Performance. Other topics relating to professionalism, such as intellectual property issues, preventing from corruption behavior, handling of privacy/personal data, etc. will also be covered in this course.To apply for the Nutritionist stream (FNS-NS), students must pass the course with at least a C in this course along with other FNS-NS admission requirements.
outcome: After completion of this course, students will be able to: analyze what is and what is not professional behaviour, remember and understand the standards of ethics, conduct and performance set by AfN, describe intellectual property issues, how to avoid corruption, and property ways of handling privacy data

Emphasis will be made on the chemical reactions and changes in these food constituents during processing, handling and storage. The principles and applications of chemical and instrumental analysis of food will be illustrated. The actions and applications of enzymes in food manufacture and food spoilage will be discussed.

title: Food Science Laboratory II
requirements: Pre-requisite: FNSC4110. Co-requisite: FNSC4170.
description: This is an integrated laboratory course for the food product production, which is composed of three interrelated areas, namely, food processing technology, food product development and food quality control. title: Community Nutrition
description: Community nutrition recognizes that the control and prevention of nutrition problems are not merely biomedical in nature, but are embedded in the community of the affected individuals. A community nutritionist assesses and monitors not only physiological and dietary, but also social, cultural, technological and psychological information from many sources to determine needs and identify opportunities for sound, appropriate interventions that improve nutritional health. Because well-conceived nutrition surveys are basic tools for prioritising problems and deciding program plans and evaluations to provide better nutrition services to the public, the course will first introduce community nutrition survey design to the students. Making healthier choices, however, requires lifelong change in thinking and action at both individual and community levels. The rest of the course examines applications of current individual and group nutritional behaviour change theories to promote healthier diets.
outcome: -Discuss the work of community nutrition in preventing disease and promoting health -Design a nutrition survey, demonstrating appropriate use of methodology and statistics -Discover findings, and arragne, interpret and present results from a nutrition survey -Appreciate the interrelationships of social, cultural, technological and psychological factors in determining food choice and eating habits -Describe how to apply some theoretical models of individual, interpersonal, and group health behaviors to designing nutrition intervention strategies
syllabus: -Community nutrition and nutrition survey research -Nutrition promotion and nutrition behavior change theories

title: Introduction to Medical Nutrition Therapy
description: Medical nutrition therapy examines the theory and practice behind the prevention and treatment of diseases with the help of diet. This course will introduce the etiology and dietary management of selected diet-related diseases including obesity; anorexia and other eating disorders; diabetes mellitus; cardiovascular diseases including hyperlipidemias; diseases of the alimentary canal, liver, kidney and gall bladder; pancreatitis; food allergy and cancer. It will also cover nutritional management for AIDS patients, interaction of drugs and nutrients, and aspects of dietary therapy in Chinese Medicine. The related applied aspects of dietetics, including the practical skills associated with the preparation, use and evaluation of special diets, and the development of interview and communication skills, will also be covered.
outcome: After taking this course, students are expected to be able to: 1. assess the nutritional status using simple nutritional assessment methods 2. distinguish between enteral nutrition and parenteral nutrition as nutritional support for patients with special needs 3. recognize the interactions between drugs and nutrients and how these interactions affect nutrition therapy 4. describe the etiology, treatment and dietary management of selected diet-related diseases including obesity and   diabetes mellitus; diseases of the heart, blood vessels, and lungs; gastrointestinal diseases, renal diseases,   food allergy and food intolerance, cancer and AIDS 5. discuss the role of Chinese Medicine as an alternate means of dietary therapy for some common diseases
syllabus: Major topics to be covered include: - Nutritional Assessment and Patient Care - Enteral and Parenteral Nutrition - Drug-Nutrient Interaction - Renal Diseases - Surgery Patients and Gastrointestinal Diseases - Medical Nutrition Therapy for Food Allergy  - Nutritional Care for Cancer Patients  - Medical Nutrition Therapy for HIV Infection and AIDS  - Obesity: Energy Imbalance - Diabetes Mellitus - Diseases of the Heart, Blood Vessels, and Lungs - Aspect of Dietary Therapy in Chinese Medicine (This topic will be taught in Cantonese)  授課內容包括以下題目： - 營養評估與病人護理 - 腸外與腸內營養  - 藥品和營養的相互作用  - 腎臟疾病  - 外科手術病人及胃腸道疾病  - 醫學營養治療食物過敏 - 癌症病人的營養護理 - 醫學營養治療HIV病毒感染及愛滋病 - 肥胖症與能量不平衡 - 糖尿病 - 心臟、血管、和肺部疾病 - 中醫食療 (此課題將會以粵語教授)

title: Nutrition Planning and Food Policy
requirements: Pre-requisite: FNSC4120.
description: This course explores the emergence of food and nutrition policies from their multisectoral agricultural, population, health, environmental, economic, technological and political origins. The class will examine case studies from the international arena, focusing on Asian regional and local food and nutrition policy developments. Because nutrition promotion to the public is an integral component of these policies, a final portion of this course is devoted to the design of effective nutrition promotion and communication strategies for specific groups, including needs assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation.

title: Food Toxicology & Safety
requirements:
For students in MSc Nutrition, Food Science and Technology or MPhil-PhD Food and Nutritional Sciences or BSc Food and Nutritional Sciences
Not for students who have taken LSCI5843
description: Food can be contaminated at any stage of its production and handling with naturally occurring toxicants and/or man-made chemicals that have adverse health effects to humans. The objective of this course is to gain knowledge on the key concepts and principles of food safety and toxicology. Students are expected to develop an understanding of the nature and properties of the toxic substances in foods as well as the nature and magnitude of the hazard they represent to humans, with the aim of preventing health risks due to food intake. Topics on food safety include food hygiene, food poisoning, food legislation and food safety control systems. Topics on food toxicology include its general principles, biochemical and physiological mechanisms of action of food toxicants, and methods for food safety assessment. Emphasis will be placed on the evaluation of current issues in food safety toxicology including risk assessment and management.
outcome: After taking this course, students are expected to be able to: 1. gain knowledge on the key concepts and principles of food safety and toxicology 2. understand the nature and properties of the toxic substances in foods as well as the nature and magnitude of the hazard they represent to humans,  3. understand the general principles, biochemical and physiological mechanisms of action of food toxicants, and methods for food safety assessment 4. understand the basic principles of food hygiene and food poisoning to prevent health risks due to food intake.  5. understand food legislation and food safety control systems, as well as risk analysis
